drop writes state: dropped into the issue on the branch you are on, with the
reason and the resolution the schema requires.

dropped on its own cannot tell a duplicate from a won't-fix, and the difference
is the first thing anyone asks — so --resolution is required and is one of
wontfix, duplicate, works-as-intended or fixed-elsewhere.

Usage:
  isu drop <id> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help                help for drop
      --reason string       why, in a sentence (required)
      --resolution string   wontfix, duplicate, works-as-intended or fixed-elsewhere (required)

Global Flags:
      --fetch         update remote refs before reading
      --json          print newline-delimited JSON instead of text
      --no-color      never colour the output
      --ref string    the ref isu treats as trunk (default: main, else master, else HEAD)
      --repo string   the repository to read (default: the working directory)
